- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model often overreacts and forecasts too high; cap forecast at 2–3% above recent peak.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and price is trending down, model frequently undercorrects; add 1–2% upward bias to prevent premature bottoming.
- Model tends to lag mean reversion by 2–3 days; if sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish, adjust forecast 1–2 days ahead to reflect reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates late-period volatility; increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for final 5–7 days if sentiment remains positive.
- If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is volatile, model over-smooths; use 1–2% higher forecast for 3rd–5th day of forecast horizon.
